key_insight: Growing Harness turns repeated agent control decisions into reusable executable code, so the LLM focuses on task-specific reasoning instead of rebuilding strategy in every context.
engineering_relevance: This can substantially cut inference cost and improve robustness for deployed agents, especially when smaller models must handle long-running streams of related tasks.
method: Start from a strategy-free scaffold with fixed model and tool interfaces.
Use function-level execution traces to localize failures, then repair a window of failures jointly.
Keep only edits that pass a success-first held-out gate; accepted fixes accumulate in one shared harness.
evidence_signal: Across BrowseComp-Plus and WebArena-Verified with 4B to 120B deployment models, the method achieved the best mean success in 5 of 6 settings and reduced LLM calls by 76.0–91.8% versus Tool-Calling.
watch_item: Because the harness is grown by failure-guided edits, performance depends on trace quality, rollback policy, and whether the learned control generalizes beyond the evaluated task streams.
paper_title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
